review.summary: AgentBench introduces an interactive benchmark spanning eight text-based environments and reports evaluations of 25 API and open models. Its breadth, task-specific execution environments, and released evaluation toolkit make it a useful contribution; the results provide evidence of a large performance gap between the tested commercial and open models. The findings are best read within the paper’s stated scope: its first-edition tasks, model roster, and evaluation choices do not establish general agent capability across real-world settings.

observations.claim: The benchmark covers varied agent tasks, including system operation, games, household tasks, and web interaction, rather than relying on a single environment.
The evaluation reports results across 25 models and shows a marked gap between the top tested API model and most open models on the aggregate score.
The aggregate score depends on inverse average scores across the tested models, so its weighting may not transfer unchanged to later model rosters.
observations.quote: we utilize the reciprocal of the average score of all the tested LLMs in each task as a weight

observations.claim: The paper acknowledges that the LTP automatic evaluator can be more lenient than human evaluation, leaving uncertainty about the reliability of some reported LTP metrics.
observations.quote: automatic evaluation sometimes more tolerate for the agent

unresolved_questions: How stable are the model rankings and aggregate scores across repeated runs, alternative prompt choices, and changes to the model roster?
How much do LTP scores change when evaluated by human judges rather than the automatic system, particularly for open-source models?

How well do these results generalize beyond the selected tasks, model sizes, and text-only interaction settings? I inspected the supplied paper text and appendices, but not external materials or underlying evaluation artifacts.
